decision.reasons: One espadin mezcal entered four times by three catalogue waves. The May-31 floor row is the canonical: it is the line staff count on both venues' latest sheets (3.6 AA, 2.8 StA on 1 Oct), it carries the continuous 2026 count history at both venues, and it is fully configured (cost, category, bottle unit). The May-3 rows exist only for the 2025 historical sheets and the 13 recipe lines, which the merge repoints; the Aug-3 Espadin row was created by one Loaded import whose wording ('Aguas Mansas Espadin') did not alias-match, and its only count (6.65) was superseded by the Aug-31 and Oct-1 counts of the same shelf. Staff behaviour on the 1 Oct AA sheet (adjacent lines, one filled, one blank) confirms they see one product.
decision.risks: (1) Bottle size: 750 vs 700 mL cannot be settled from data (no invoice lines; Loaded labelled it 750 mL in June and 700 mL in August). Check a bottle on the shelf and set the canonical's measurePerCountUnit accordingly; until then the 13 repointed recipe lines cost ~7% lower per mL than before. (2) The Espadin holding (6.65, $432) is discarded on the strength of the 31/08 and 01/10 Bar & FOH counts naming only 'Aguas Mansas'; if St Alma kept a separate Espadin stash off those sheets, that stock would be unrecorded - a quick shelf glance at St Alma rules this out. (3) Run the merge before applying the 1 Oct sheets so the blank Espadin line folds into the canonical's line; applying afterwards sets AA 3.6 / StA 2.8. (4) The 'Also known as' wordings on the May-3 rows are free-text notes, not aliases; if supplier invoices ever read 'AGUAS MANSAS 700ML BOTTLE' or '(CASE OF 6)', add those as aliases on the canonical so auto-matching does not recreate a duplicate. (5) The cancelled PO line and the resolved reorder notice repoint harmlessly; the twins' venue par levels (6 StA on the case row, 4 AA on the bottle row) are dropped with their holding rows - the canonical already has pars 7 / 6.

verdicts.reasoning: Product identity holds. In alma_stock_orig, only four StockItems match 'mansas': the four cluster members. Every other mezcal row with 'Espadin' in its name belongs to another brand (El Jolgorio, Madre, Gracias a Dios, Koch), so no second Aguas Mansas expression is being collapsed. Aguas Mansas is the brand and Espadin is its expression; the Aug-3 row 'Aguas Mansas Espadin' was created from one Loaded count (note: 'Added from the Loaded count of Sat 1st Aug') and its alias is the same wording. Pack: the (CASE OF 6) row has unit=case and conversionFactor 6, but countUnit is bottle and its cost is per bottle (6500), so it is the same bottle bought by the case. Its free-text notes include the 'aguas mansas 700ml case of 6' wording, and the 700ML BOTTLE row's notes give the same 'aguas mansas' wordings. The cost is the same on all four rows (6500/6500/6502/6505), and no row has a supplier or invoice lines that would show a different product. Bottle size: three rows say 700 mL. The canonical says 750 mL, and Loaded labelled its June lines '750 mL'. This is a metadata conflict on one SKU, not two SKUs. Two sizes at the same per-bottle price, with one continuous count series per venue, would be implausible. The 700 mL rows are the invoice-style and later Loaded-derived records, so 700 mL is more likely correct. The decision already flags this as risk (1). Recommended follow-up (not grounds to refute): set the canonical's measurePerCountUnit to 700 after a shelf check, so the 13 repointed mL recipe lines are not costed about 7% low. The count series join up with no overlapping non-null counts on any real-venue sheet. On the 1 Oct Alma Avalon sheet the Espadin line was left blank next to the filled Aguas Mansas line, which supports staff seeing one product. Nothing points to a vintage, a different expression, a different strength or a different supplier product. Keep-separate list: none.

(a) Canonical cmptovvht006cs601a21zsvns is the only member counted on both latest real-venue sheets (AA 'Stocktake 10/1/2026' 3.6; StA 'Bar & FOH 01/10/2026' 2.8) and carries category, bottle count unit, factor 1 and cost 6505. Correct choice. (b) Values check: 0.95x6505=6180, 4.1x6505=26670, 6.1x6500=39650, 4.4x6500=28600, 6.65x6502=43238. Discarded 39650+28600+43238=111488, retained 6180+26670=32850. All match. Each discarded holding is stale: case row StA last counted 2025-12-31, then superseded by canonical counts 2026-03-31, 31/08 and 01/10. Bottle row AA last counted 2025-12-31, then superseded by canonical 06-02, 06-30, 9/1 and 10/1. Espadin StA's only count was the 3 Aug Loaded sheet, where the canonical had no line, and the 31/08 and 01/10 StA sheets count the shelf as the canonical. The null holdings (bottle@StA, Espadin@AA) add 0 and get deleted. After the merge: AA 0.95 and StA 4.1, becoming 3.6 and 2.8 once the 1 Oct sheets are applied. (c) No real sheet has two non-null counts. On AA 10/1, mergeItems folds the blank Espadin line (unit bottle = bottle) as 3.6+0 = 3.6 and deletes it. The code folds on any stocktake status, so the result is right with treatment none. The historical sheets have only one member per venue. VOID and phantom are excluded (and their unit labels 'ml' vs '750 mL' would block the fold anyway). (d) All members count in bottles, so summed and repointed counts are safe. The one real gap is measurePerCountUnit: canonical 750 vs 700 on all three twins. mergeItems only backfills a NULL, so the 13 repointed mL recipe lines drop from 9.29c to 8.67c per mL. The evidence leans toward 700: the supplier-invoice name says '700ML', the case-row note says 'Pack: 4200 ml' (6x700), the Aug Loaded row says 700, and 700 mL is the AU spirits norm. The decision discloses this as risk 1 with a shelf check, so I am not refuting it. Strongly recommended amendment: set the canonical's measurePerCountUnit to 700 at merge time unless the shelf shows 750. (e) Costs 6500/6500/6502/6505 are within 2x, and the case row's cost is already per bottle, so no cost treatment is needed.

The twin cmoqfbqhg00fg9ky23y8bv1fv 'MEZCAL VERDE MOMENTO 700ML BOTTLE' records 'Also known as: mezcal verde / Mezcal Verde' in its notes. Its 'Mezcal Verde'-labelled 2025 historical lines carry on directly into the canonical cmptovwi300e6s6012ryyx12w's 2026 counts with the same level of stock: St Alma 1.8-1.85 in Aug-Dec 2025, then 1.7 in Jun-Oct 2026; Alma Avalon 0.6-0.8, then 0.65-0.7. The Loaded import uses both '700 mL' (377 lines) and '750 mL' (670 lines), so its '750 mL' on the canonical's lines is a deliberate entry and not a default, while the May name says 700ML. That is a label-size question about one product, and the decision already flags it (confirm the label; if it is 700, set measurePerCountUnit to 700). It is not grounds to keep the items separate. The 9 mis-attached lines on the twin (5 Machetazo-labelled, 4 kitchen prep Verde lines) are correctly named as risks and are not a second Verde Momento product. Minor point: because Loaded really does tell 700 from 750, the size check should be done before the recipe costing is relied on, not left as optional.

identity.differences: Same brand and expression (Jameson Irish Whiskey, the standard blend; no age statement, no vintage, no pack suffix). No supplier evidence on either member: 0 invoice lines, 0 price-list rows, no supplier on any alias, and the only purchase order (CANCELLED, Alma Avalon 27 Aug 2026, 'No known supplier') lists both. The one real difference checked is bottle size, and it is conflicting metadata rather than evidence of two bottlings: the May record is named '1000ML BOTTLE' with measurePerCountUnit 1000 and avgCost 7754 (its notes store cost per ml 0.07754); the floor record has measurePerCountUnit 750 while its own notes say 'Cost taken from the Loaded count (drinks.json): 1 700 mL = $54.28' and its Loaded import lines (St Alma 2026-03-31/06-02/06-30, Alma Avalon 06-02/06-30) carry the unit '700 mL'. The two costs are exactly proportional (5428 = 0.7 x 7754, per-ml 0.07754 on both), so one was derived from the other; the 2025 Historical Bar Stocktake sheets valued the bottle at 8529-8530c = 7754 x 1.1 (the 1 L price inc GST) and the floor record's own latestCostCents is 7760 (31 May 2026), so the independently sourced price is the 1 L one and Loaded's $54.28 is a pro-rata, which points to the venue buying 1 L bottles (the audit's naming guide already uses 'Jameson Irish Whiskey 1L' as its example). What settles identity regardless of size: every sheet from Aug 2025 to Oct 2026 carries exactly ONE Jameson line per venue and the quantity is continuous (St Alma 1/1/1/1/1 on the 2025 sheets, 0.5 on 31 Mar 2026, 1 on 2 Jun, 30 Jun, 1 Aug, 31 Aug and 1 Oct 2026; Alma Avalon 0.5/0.5/0.4/0.5/0.45 in 2025, 0.5 on 2 Jun and 30 Jun, 0.38 on 1 Sep, 0.47 on 1 Oct 2026); a 700 mL and a 1 L Jameson never appear side by side, and the May record's notes list the floor name as an alias ('Also known as: jameson • Jameson • jameson irish whiskey • Jameson Irish Whiskey'). One product counted under two records; the bottle size is a field to correct on the survivor, not a second product.

Its one defect (measurePerCountUnit 750, contradicted by its own notes) is a single field to correct after a label check and does not outweigh count-sheet continuity; choosing the May twin instead would carry the probably-correct 1 L metadata but would also carry its supplier-style name and 13 mis-mapped lines. The May twin has no 2026 count on any real sheet, no invoice lines, no alias row; its only live value is a July-2026 replay of the Sept-2025 count. Same brand, same expression, one Jameson line per sheet with a continuous quantity from Aug 2025 into Oct 2026, costs that are arithmetically one price, and the twin's notes naming the floor name as an alias: one product under two records. Merging repoints the twin's 26 stocktake lines, 2 recipe lines, 24 movements, 1 PO line and 2 reorder notices onto the canonical, losing nothing. Name: 'Jameson Irish Whiskey'; per the audit's own naming guide rename to 'Jameson Irish Whiskey 1L' once the 1 L size is confirmed on the shelf.

verdicts.reasoning: Identity holds. Both records are Capi sparkling grapefruit in the Non-Alcoholic & Mixers category, counted 'each'. The only other Capi item is Capi Ginger Beer (cmptovv150036s601c09m15sy), which is correctly left out. Neither name carries a size, expression or variant marker. '(CASE OF 12)' is the purchase pack, not a different product. Neither record has invoice lines, aliases or price lists. The May record's aliases in its notes ('capi grapefruit soda', 'Capi Grapefruit Soda') and its two recipe lines (Paloma and Mango Grapefruit Fresca, 75 ml each, St Alma) describe the same mixer. The count history reads like one product handed between two records, not two formats stocked side by side. Alma Avalon: floor item 17 on 2 Jun and 28 on 30 Jun (Loaded), then the May item 2 on 1 Sep and 10 on 1 Oct. On the 1 Oct sheet the floor line is blank. St Alma: floor item 32.5 on 31 Mar, May item 0 on 1 Aug, floor item 0 on 31 Aug. No real sheet has non-zero counts on both. One caveat about pack size, which is a costing issue and not a reason to keep the records apart. The May record's size evidence contradicts itself. measurePerCountUnit says 250 ml. Its notes say 'Pack: 9000 ml' (12 x 750 ml, or 36 x 250 ml). The recipe-line unit cost of 0.3746 c/ml is 4495/12000, which implies 12 x 1 L. Loaded's 197c per bottle fits a 250 ml bottle (a 24 x 250 ml carton at about $45 is about 187c each). Nothing suggests the venues stocked a large-format Capi alongside the 250 ml bottle: there are no concurrent counts on both records, the counts are of similar size, and Capi grapefruit is normally sold as 250 ml bottles. So treating them as one product is sound. The decision already flags the case-size/cost doubt. Its risk note should also mention the 9000 ml note and the per-ml recipe cost, so that after the merge the parent's conversionFactor (12) and recipe costing are checked against the next invoice.

Making cmoqfb canonical, against the floor-named default, is justified: it has the correct 5000 g measure and cost, and it carries all 3 recipe lines in g/kg. The default parent cmptow would keep its non-null 100 g measure and mis-cost those lines. Nothing needs to stay separate.

verdicts.reasoning: Only two dill records exist in the catalogue (cmoqfbnx3009k9ky2oav6wpwa 'Dill', cmptowbho00v8s6015b4wn135 'Dill Bunch'). I tried to refute on the theory that 'Dill' is dried dill: its notes say 'Storage: Dry Store'. That does not hold up. The May-wave import puts 'Storage: Dry Store' on fresh herb bunches too (Continental Parsley Bunch and Thyme Bunch both have 'Pack: 1 units | Cost per each: 2-2.5 | Storage: Dry Store'). Dried herbs in that wave are always sold by weight with a gram pack in the name or notes (Thyme Leaves 200GM, Mexican Oregano 250g, Confetti Coriander 50 gram). Dill has 'Pack: 1 units, Cost per each: 2', exactly the fresh-bunch pattern. Its 2025 historical kitchen counts were valued at 266c per unit, close to Dill Bunch's 238-285c per bunch, so one 'each' is one bunch. There is no size, variety or supplier difference, and neither item has invoices, recipes or aliases that suggest otherwise. The 100 g vs 30 g measurePerCountUnit difference is a configuration guess and does not make them different products. The canonical choice (Dill Bunch, the floor-named item counted on the latest Alma Avalon sheet) is sound. Same product, same pack: the merge stands.

verdicts.reasoning: Product identity checks. All three items have countUnit bottle and 750 mL per bottle. Wark Family Shiraz is a different wine from the other Teusner items (Big Jim, Avatar GSM, The G, Righteous FG), so the cluster is correct at the wine level. The only identity question is vintage. The floor item has no year. Its 1383c cost sits closer to the 2023's 1400c than to the 2022's 1695c, but 1383 is not equal to 1400, and cost is the decision's only evidence that the floor item is the 2023. Every other piece of evidence says the vintage labels are import artefacts, not distinct stock. (a) The history split follows spelling, not vintage. St Alma's 'Teusner' lines went to the 2022 and Avalon's 'Tesuner' lines went to the 2023. Both carry the identical 2025 valuation of about 1865c a bottle (e.g. 27975/15 and 51926/27.85). (b) The recipes are undated and identical in name: 'Teusner Wark Family Shiraz 750mL' at St Alma sits on the 2022, and Avalon's 150/250/750 mL sit on the 2023. So the venues sell one undated product. (c) The floor item holds the stock that BOTH vintaged records held. At St Alma its 15.2 (Loaded, 31 Mar 2026) continues the 2022's count of 15 in Sep, Oct and Nov 2025. At Avalon its 8.9 and 14.9 continue the 2023 history. The decision itself uses (c) to discard the 2022's St Alma 15 as 'the same bin counted under the floor item'. That admits the floor item and the 2022 are the same stock, which contradicts keeping the 2022 as a separate product and contradicts naming the canonical '2023'. (d) On AA 1 Oct staff entered 0 on both vintaged items and 14.9 on the floor item. This treats the floor item as THE Wark Family whatever its year, not as the 2023 only. (e) PO of 27 Aug 2026 orders both the floor item (1 bottle at 1383c) and the 2023 (3 cases) for the same product. That is a duplicate-reorder symptom, not two products. Keeping the 2022 separate as planned leaves a live duplicate: it has a line on the current AA sheet, an active St Alma recipe costed at 1695c for the same menu item, and its holding is zeroed. The vintage rule is meant to protect genuinely different stock. Here the floor catalogue (the only one counted since mid-2026) does not track vintage, so the defensible options are an undated merge of all three, or no merge until the bottles are checked. The partial merge with a '2023' name is neither. Mis-mapped history checks out on value: Avatar 16177/6 = 2696c (Avatar avg 2451c) and Big Jim 25073/6 = 4179c (Big Jim avg 3799c). Those lines belong to cmptovvg40060s60123zb2ouq and cmsdf10os007rmiiocxqo2ss2 respectively and must not be carried onto the Wark canonical.

verdicts.reasoning: PRODUCT IDENTITY: upheld. I found no evidence that these are different products. (1) Vintage: both invoice items say 2022 in the name. The floor item has no year, and no other BenMarco vintage exists anywhere in the catalogue. (2) Size: all three are countUnit bottle at 750 ml. The '(Case of 6)' / Pack 4500 ml on the two invoice items is only the purchase pack (conversionFactor 6, the same on both). (3) Expression: a catalogue search of alma_stock_orig for benmarco/ben marco/susana/malbec/gaucho finds only these three items plus the unrelated Wendouree Cabernet Malbec. There is no BenMarco Expresivo or Sin Limites, and no Susana Balbo item. 'Valle de Uco' is the appellation printed on the standard BenMarco Malbec label, not a separate cuvee. The audit note's worry, 'Valle de Uco vs standard Malbec', is therefore a false distinction. (4) Cross-evidence: the two invoice items' 'Also known as' notes name each other ('BenMarco Valle de Uco Malbec' on the Malbec item, 'BenMarco Malbec' on the Valle de Uco item). AA's 2025 historical lines on cmoqfbk55 are labelled 'BenMarco Valle de Uco Malbec', while StA's lines on cmoqfbk60 are labelled 'BenMarco Malbec'. Both venues valued the bottle at exactly 2774c (AA 08.25 44107/15.9; StA 08.25 38281/13.8). Each item feeds the same three recipe names ('BenMarco Malbec 150/250/750mL'), one item per venue. The floor item's counts continue those series: StA 13.9 on 2 Jun, 15.8 on 30 Jun, 12.9 on 3 Aug and 12 on 1 Oct; AA 9.3 on 2 Jun, 13.7 on 30 Jun, 7 on 1 Sep and 3.7 on 1 Oct. Only one argument points the other way: the May supplier costs differ, 1975c vs 2293c a bottle. That 16% gap fits two price lists or dates for one wine, not two wines, and is outweighed by the identical 2025 valuations. Caveat, not a refutation: three 2025 StA historical lines on cmoqfbk60 are labelled 'Gaucho Malbec' (Aug 6, Sep 10, Oct 6 bottles, valued at 1277c a bottle). That is a different, cheaper wine mis-mapped onto this item. No Gaucho StockItem exists in the catalogue, so the merge will carry those lines onto the canonical as history. Flag them for repointing or re-labelling if a Gaucho item is ever created, but they do not affect the identity of the three members. The canonical choice of cmptovvay (the floor item, on the latest sheet at both venues, correctly configured as bottle/750ml/cf 1) is sound. Nothing needs to stay separate.

verdicts.reasoning: (a) Canonical: neither box item has a count on the latest AA sheet (1 Oct SUBMITTED, null lines; tomatoes were counted there on the kg floor item). On the latest finalised St Alma kitchen sheet (31/8) Large Box holds the real count (0.474) and LRG holds 0. Strictly, the latest-sheet rule picks Large Box. But its measurePerCountUnit of 100 g is wrong for a 10 kg box, and backfill only fills empty fields, so the 100 g would survive. Picking LRG (10000 g) is justified. Category Prod, countUnit each and cost are present on both. (b) The AA LRG holding of 1 box was last counted Nov 2025 and is absent from the 3 Aug and 1 Oct AA sheets, so discard is right (6480 = 1 x 6480). The St Alma figures are where the decision goes wrong. Both onHands come from applying the 31/8 sheet on 2 Oct, as loose count plus raw tomato held in counted prep batches. LRG's 0.431 is correctly scaled and is backed by the count, so discarding it as 'not backed by any count' is wrong. Large Box's 0.758 is not drift: 0.284 of it is a prep share inflated 100x by the 100 g measure. 'Recount' and carrying 0.758 would store the inflated figure, and the discard throws away the correctly scaled prep share. The decision's arithmetic (9273 / 44701) adds up, but it is built on those two misreadings. (c) Same-sheet: on 31/8 LRG = 0 and Large Box = 0.474, the same box under two labels with one blank, so keep_duplicate_line is right. The historical sheets never overlap (AA lines are on LRG only, St Alma lines on Large Box only). The AA 1 Oct SUBMITTED sheet will end up with two null LRG lines after repointing. There is no unique index on (stocktakeId, itemId), so nothing fails, but the duplicate null line should be dropped. (d) Units: both box items count in 'each' (one box). Repointing Large Box's 12 St Alma gram recipes onto LRG at 10000 g fixes their ~100x overcosting. The floor kg item is rightly kept separate. (e) Costs: 6480 vs 3550 is 1.83x, under the 2x threshold. Resetting to the latest invoice price of 4560 is sensible, and costReviewed false is acceptable.
